idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api health check failures on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 18% with healthy=false reported by the service status. Mitigation: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production (released healthy at seq 1). The first rollback attempt halted with a partial failure after us-east (orchestrator error), leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry of the same rollback completed across all three regions. Post-rollback verification shows all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the health check failure is root-caused; the rollout of v2.3.1 also appears to have left a staging RC (v2.3.1-rc) in an unhealthy state. Further investigation needed to determine the cause of the v2.3.1 failure and the orchestrator partial-failure error during rollback.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Investigation**
- `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three production regions with `healthy: false` and an 18% error rate.
- Release history showed the most recent production-healthy release was **v2.3.0** (seq 1), with v2.3.1 (seq 3) unhealthy and a staging RC `v2.3.1-rc` also unhealthy.

**Rollback**
- First attempt to v2.3.0 failed partway: `partial_failure — rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`. Verified state showed us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west were still on the unhealthy v2.3.1.
- Retried the rollback; it completed across all regions. Verified: us-east/us-west/eu-west all on **v2.3.0**, `healthy: true`, error rate down to **0.2%**.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for `checkout-api`, paged on-call. The first create call timed out with unknown outcome, so I retried with the same idempotency key; confirmed exactly one incident exists, so no duplicate page was sent.
- The incident summary documents the v2.3.1 failure, the completed rollback to v2.3.0, the mid-rollback orchestrator error, and recommends root-causing v2.3.1 before any redeploy.

Note: this was a rollback to a version previously healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was required. Deploying v2.3.1 again would require change-manager approval and should wait on root cause.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the current status and release history for checkout-api.
Current state: v2.3.1 is unhealthy across all three regions (18% error rate). The most recent production-healthy release is v2.3.0. Rolling back now.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Current v2.3.1 unhealthy in all regions. Most recent healthy in production: v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1-rc is staging, not production.

Rollback to v2.3.0. Rollback to a previously released healthy version — rollback doesn't require change-manager approval (that's for deploying a version never healthy in production). So rollback is fine.

Then create SEV2 incident.

transcript.content: The rollback hit an orchestrator error partway through. Let me check the actual state before retrying.
transcript.reasoning_content: The rollback partially failed. Let me check the current status to see what's going on.

transcript.content: Partial state: us-east is on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on unhealthy v2.3.1. Retrying the rollback to complete the remaining regions.
transcript.reasoning_content:
us-east is now v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west are still v2.3.1. I need to complete the rollout to remaining regions. The deploy tool deploys a version to all production regions. But deploy is for deploying a version — is deploying v2.3.0 the same as completing a rollback? Deploying v2.3.0 to all regions would complete it. Policy: deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires approval. v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, so no approval needed.

But wait — the rollback tool is the appropriate one. Retrying rollback is idempotent-ish and would target remaining regions. Let's retry rollback to v2.3.0 to complete the remaining regions.

Actually, deploy v2.3.0 would also set all regions to v2.3.0. But rollback is semantically correct and commercial: rollback rolls back to previously released version in all production regions. Retry rollback.

transcript.content: All regions now on v2.3.0 and healthy (error rate 0.2%). Opening the SEV2 incident.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Now open a SEV2 incident. Note policy: deploying a version never healthy in production requires change-manager approval. We used rollback to v2.3.0 which was healthy before, so no approval needed.

Create incident with idempotency key.
